__comment: Phase 16 — Grafana dashboard over the OTel traces core/otel.py exports. Import: Grafana -> Dashboards -> New -> Import -> Upload JSON, then pick your Tempo datasource. Every panel is a TraceQL metrics query; there is no Prometheus side to configure. TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE QUERY BUGS AND ARE NOT: turn-latency panels filter span.turn.held = false, because a HELD turn (the caller paused mid-sentence and core/endpointing.py bought them grace) has no reply and its span runs until they speak again — including those measures how long callers think, not how fast the agent is; and the filter is written = false rather than != true because TraceQL does not match a span that LACKS the attribute, which is why otel.py emits turn.held on every turn instead of only when set.
title: Clinic Voice Agent

panels.title: Latency — the number a caller actually feels
Voice-to-voice per turn (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: SpeechStopped -> BotStartedSpeaking, the same boundary every latency number in this project uses. span.turn.held = false excludes turns where the caller paused mid-sentence and core/endpointing.py bought them grace: those have no reply, so their span runs until the caller speaks again and would measure how long callers think. Written `= false` rather than `!= true` because TraceQL does not match a span that LACKS the attribute. Phase-14 exit criterion: p50 <= 1200 ms, p95 <= 2000 ms.

panels.title: Per stage, p95 — which stage is the slow one
panels.description: The whole point of splitting the turn. A single voice-to-voice number cannot say whether a slow call is the model, the endpointer, or the speech queue, and those have completely different fixes. Measured 2026-09-04, LLM TTFT was ~50% of every turn.

panels.title: Tools — did the thing the agent said it did actually happen
Tool failures
panels.description: A 403, 404 or 409 is an ANSWER, not a failure — wrong DOB, no such appointment, slot just taken — and the model handles all three in dialogue. What matters here is tool.ok=false, and a sustained rise in it is what the Phase-15 degradation ladder reacts to.

panels.title: Tool latency p95 by endpoint
panels.description: Anchored backwards from ToolCompleted's measured latency_ms — there is no ToolStarted event, and inventing one would mean a second source of truth for the same number.

panels.title: Calls — volume, intent, and what went wrong
Calls by intent
panels.description: The intent classified on the MOST turns of the call, ignoring `unknown`. Taking the last classification instead labelled every call `unknown`, because the last thing a caller says is "thanks, bye". The reducer's sticky intent is the true answer and is not in the event stream, so this is the closest a pure mapper can get.

panels.title: Bookings completed
panels.description: call.booked is set only by a confirm_booking tool call the API accepted. It is deliberately NOT set by anything the model said: the worst failure this system can have is a caller hanging up believing they have an appointment, and a booking counter sourced from speech would count exactly those.

panels.title: Provider degradation + failed transfers
panels.description: ProviderDegraded with fatal=false is one socket blipping while the adapter reconnects; fatal=true means it is not coming back and the call goes to a person. A failed transfer is the worst of both — the caller was promised a human and the hand-off did not happen.

panels.title: Endpointing grace held
panels.description: core/endpointing.py holds the turn when the caller pauses mid-sentence. Measured across 14 calls it is 90% precise and costs 5.5 s total; a sustained rise here means Deepgram's 300 ms window is cutting people off more often, which is a change in caller behaviour or in the audio path, not in this code.

panels.title: Barge-ins per call
panels.description: The caller interrupting the agent. Some of this is healthy; a spike is usually the agent being too wordy or the endpointer answering a fragment.
